gloss: to lose out; to be worse off; to take a loss

definitions.gloss: to lose out; to be worse off; to take a loss
definitions.explanation: To end up worse off than one otherwise would — paying more, wasting effort, or missing an advantage. The direct opposite of {得|とく}をする.

examples.japanese: ⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{損|そん}をする。
examples.english: You lose out if you don't know about it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{慌|あわ}てて→慌てる：01874_awateru⟧⟦{売|う}った→売る：00906_uru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{十万円|じゅうまんえん}{損|そん}をした。
examples.english: I sold in a hurry and lost a hundred thousand yen.

examples.japanese: ⟦{断|ことわ}り→断る：02102_kotowaru⟧きれない⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{損|そん}をして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I can never say no, and I always feel like I'm the one losing out.

examples.japanese: {短期的|たんきてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{損|そん}をして⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{信用|しんよう}→信用：03267_shinyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}った→守る：01986_mamoru⟧ほう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}れば→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦{有利|ゆうり}→有利：03651_yuuri⟧だ。
examples.english: Even if you take a loss in the short term, protecting your credibility pays off in the long run.

notes:
The loss is often financial, but the phrase covers any disadvantage — wasted time, unfair treatment, or a missed opportunity. ⟦{損|そん}→損：03325_son⟧ also works as a na-adjective (⟦{損|そん}→損：03325_son⟧な{役回|やくまわ}り, a thankless role).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ...⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{損|そん}をする: you lose out if you don't ...
- {損|そん}をした⟦{気分|きぶん}→気分：01306_kibun⟧: the feeling of having been shortchanged
- {損|そん}して{得|とく}⟦{取|と}れ→取る：00565_toru⟧: take a small loss to win a bigger gain (proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{得|とく}をする→得をする：30190_tokuwosuru⟧: to come out ahead — the direct opposite
- {損|そん}する: the same phrase with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ dropped, common in casual speech
- ⟦{赤字|あかじ}→赤字：04712_akaji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to go into the red — specifically about accounts running a deficit
